title: Behavior trees
summary: How a tree runs: ticks, RUNNING, SUCCESS and FAILURE, Sequence, Fallback and Timeout.

steps.title: A tree of steps
steps.say: A behavior tree is a to-do list with a few rules. Each box is a step, and boxes that hold other boxes decide **how** to run them. About fifty times a second the robot goes through the tree once; that pass is called a *tick*.

board.code:
Sequence
  Wake up
  Eat breakfast
  Pack bag

marks.label: decides how to run what is inside

steps.title: Three answers
steps.say: Every step answers each tick with one of three things: **RUNNING** (still working), **SUCCESS** (done, it worked) or **FAILURE** (it didn't). Driving a path is RUNNING until the robot arrives, then SUCCESS.

steps.title: Sequence
steps.say: A **Sequence** does its children in order, one at a time. It moves on when a child succeeds, and stops with FAILURE the moment a child fails. 'Pack bag' never happens if 'Eat breakfast' fails.

board.code:
Sequence
  Wake up
  Eat breakfast
  Pack bag

steps.title: Fallback
steps.say: A **Fallback** is plan B. It tries its children in order and stops at the first one that **succeeds**. Only if everything fails does it fail.

marks.label: only tried if the bus fails

steps.title: Timeout
steps.say: A **Timeout** wraps one step and gives it a time limit in milliseconds. If the step is still RUNNING when time is up, the Timeout stops it and reports FAILURE. That turns 'might hang forever' into 'fails after three seconds', which a Fallback can then handle.

board.code:
Fallback
  Timeout 3000
    Aim at the goal
  Drive to the backup spot

steps.title: Tunable values
steps.say: Any number can be a **tunable**: instead of typing 500 into a Sleep, you declare a port on the tree (with a default) and write its name in braces, `{wait_msec}`. On the robot you can then change it from the dashboard without rebuilding anything.
